subject: Error in t(Delta[[g]]) %*% B1 : non-conformable arguments

messages.author: 2f40ed71ed2c3b06
messages.subject: Error in t(Delta[[g]]) %*% B1 : non-conformable arguments
parts:
Hello, lavaan team,

I got an error from sem function.

theFitMissingRobustStandardizedBidder <- sem(theModelStandardizedBidder, data=dt,
estimator="MLR", conditional.x=T)
Error in t(Delta[[g]]) %*% B1 : non-conformable arguments

But the next function works fine,

theFitMissingRobustStandardizedBidder <- sem(theModelStandardizedBidder, data=dt,
estimator="MLR")

which is wierd, because I heard it that the lavaan switches to "conditional.x=T" when there's a categorical x

and my data has a categorical x.

Can you help me figure out what's wrong?

KwH Kim

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error in t(Delta[[g]]) %*% B1 : non-conformable arguments
parts:
On 10/06/2016 05:04 PM, KwonHyun Kim wrote:
> Hello, lavaan team,
>
> I got an error from sem function.
>
> theFitMissingRobustStandardizedBidder <- sem(theModelStandardizedBidder,
> data=dt,
> estimator="MLR", conditional.x=T)
> Error in t(Delta[[g]]) %*% B1 : non-conformable arguments

This looks like a bug in lavaan 0.5-22. It occurs when estimator = "MLR"
(or "MLF") and conditional.x = TRUE. I will investigate and fix it.

> which is wierd, because I heard it that the lavaan switches to
> "conditional.x=T" when there's a categorical x
That is true, but then the estimator is "WLSMV" (by default). This works.
> and my data has a categorical x.

Is this 'x' exogenous or endogenous? You did not use the ordered=
argument in the sem() call. Perhaps lavaan did not realize this variable
was categorical?

Yves.

Thank you for answering,

x was exogenous and str(df) shows that it's a factor actually it's TRUE or FALSE from a conditional statement.

I don't think lavaan can get confused with it, anyway conditional.x applies to only exogenous variables, doesn't it?
